decisions.choice: verses 1-4 as the Hebrew text has them
alternatives: leave out verses 1-4 with the Greek
decisions.reason: The ancient Greek translation does not have verses 1-4; it moves from 16:21 straight to verse 5. The Greek of Jeremiah is shorter than the Hebrew throughout the book (see the note at 1:1), and verses 3-4 repeat 15:13-14 closely, which may be one reason the passage is missing there. The Hebrew text is followed here. This claim is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: a stylus of iron, a point of diamond: tools for cutting letters into the hardest surfaces
decisions.reason: An iron stylus was used to cut letters into stone (Job 19:24). The word translated "diamond" names a very hard stone, used in Ezekiel 3:9 of something harder than flint; it may be emery or some other hard mineral rather than the gem. The point is that Judah's sin is cut in so deep that it cannot be rubbed out.

decisions.choice: the tablet of their heart: sin written where God's law should be written
decisions.reason: The commandments were written on tablets of stone (Exodus 31:18; 34:1), and the wise are told to write God's teaching "on the tablet of your heart" (Proverbs 3:3; 7:3). Here sin is engraved there instead. Jeremiah 31:33 looks ahead to the day when God himself will write his law on his people's hearts.

decisions.choice: the horns of your altars: the corner projections where the blood of the sin offering was put
decisions.reason: An altar had a raised point, called a horn, at each corner. The priest put the blood of the sin offering on the horns to make atonement (Leviticus 4:7, 18, 25; 16:18). The word for "sin" at the start of the verse is the same word as "sin offering". Judah's altars, meant for taking sin away, now carry the record of it. The change from "their" heart to "your" altars is in the Hebrew; the prophet turns to address the people directly.

decisions.choice: like words on a stone tablet / the horns at the corners
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two pictures: a tablet was a flat stone for writing on, and the horns of an altar stood at its corners (m3, m4).

decisions.choice: "sus altares" / "vuestros altares"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew turns here from "their heart" to "your altars", plural; Spanish "sus altares" alone could be read as "their altars", so the plural you span keeps the change of person visible in the forms of Spain.

decisions.choice: as their children remember: the children keep the worship of the altars in mind as their parents did
alternatives: as they remember their children (sacrificed there)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is brief, "as their children remember". It most likely means that the next generation remembers and keeps up the false worship, so that the sin is passed down. It could also be read "as they remember their children", referring to children offered on these altars (7:31), but the word order favors the children as the ones who remember.

decisions.choice: Asherah poles beside green trees: wooden objects set up for the goddess Asherah at open-air shrines
decisions.reason: Asherah was a Canaanite goddess, and the poles or carved wooden posts named after her stood beside altars (Exodus 34:13; Deuteronomy 16:21). Shady, leafy trees on hilltops were favorite places for such worship (2:20; 3:6, 13; Deuteronomy 12:2).

decisions.choice: verses 3-4 repeat 15:13-14 with small differences
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 15:13-14 has almost the same words. There the wealth is given as plunder "without price" (bimchir), here "your high places" (bamotekha), two words that look alike in Hebrew. 15:14 says God will make the people "pass over" with their enemies, where 17:4 says he will make them "serve" their enemies, again a difference of one similar letter. Prophets repeated their own sayings, and the two forms both fit their place.

decisions.choice: my mountain in the open country: Jerusalem, God's mountain, rising from the land around it
alternatives: the mountains in the open country (ending verse 2)
decisions.reason: God calls the city "my mountain", as Zion is called his holy mountain (Isaiah 2:2-3; Psalm 2:6). Some join these words to the end of verse 2, "on the high hills, the mountains in the open country", referring to more hilltop shrines; the Hebrew accents put them with verse 3 as an address to the city.

decisions.choice: your high places, for sin: the shrines are handed over because of the sin committed at them
decisions.reason: The phrase is short and can be taken two ways: the high places are given up along with the treasures, "because of sin" throughout the land, or the high places are themselves called the sin. Either way the shrines that caused the sin are lost with everything else.

decisions.choice: You who live on my mountain / let your enemies carry off
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the city is addressed through its people and that plunder means enemies taking things away. It leaves out the name of the city, which the verse does not give.

decisions.choice: high places / hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: The settled wording for these shrines (as in Samuel and Kings).

records.literal_gloss: And you will let drop, and by yourself, from your inheritance that I gave to you; and I will make you serve your enemies in [the] land that not you know; for fire you have kindled in my anger; until forever it will burn.

en.L: And you will let go, even by yourself, of your inheritance that I gave you, \q and I will make you serve your enemies in a land that you do not know; \q for you have kindled a fire in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger; it will burn forever.
en.B: Through your own doing you will let go of the inheritance I gave you, \q and I will make you serve your enemies in a land you do not know; \q for you have set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger burning like a fire that will burn forever.
en.R: Because of what you have done, you will lose the land I gave you to keep. \q I will make you serve your enemies in a land you have never known. \q For you have lit the fire of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, and it will burn forever.

es.L: Y tú misma soltarás la heredad que te di, \q y te haré servir a tus enemigos en una tierra que no conoces; \q porque {{plural_you:han encendido|habéis encendido}} un fuego en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira; para siempre arderá.
es.B: Por tu propia culpa perderás la heredad que te di, \q y te haré servir a tus enemigos en una tierra que no conoces; \q porque {{plural_you:ustedes han encendido|vosotros habéis encendido}} {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira como un fuego que arderá para siempre.
es.R: Por lo que has hecho, perderás la tierra que te di para que la conservaras. \q Te haré servir a tus enemigos en una tierra que nunca has conocido. \q Porque {{plural_you:ustedes han encendido|vosotros habéis encendido}} el fuego de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira, y arderá para siempre.

fr.L: Et tu lâcheras, et par toi-même, ton héritage que je t’avais donné, \q et je te ferai servir tes ennemis dans un pays que tu ne connais pas ; \q car vous avez allumé un feu dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère ; il brûlera pour toujours.
fr.B: Par ta propre faute, tu lâcheras l’héritage que je t’avais donné, \q et je te ferai servir tes ennemis dans un pays que tu ne connais pas ; \q car vous avez allumé {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère comme un feu qui brûlera pour toujours.
fr.R: À cause de ce que tu as fait, tu perdras le pays que je t’avais donné à garder. \q Je te ferai servir tes ennemis dans un pays que tu n’as jamais connu. \q Car vous avez allumé le feu de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère, et il brûlera pour toujours.

sw.L: Nawe utaachilia, hata wewe mwenyewe, urithi wako niliokupa, \q nami nitakufanya uwatumikie adui zako katika nchi usiyoijua; \q kwa maana mmewasha moto katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; utawaka milele.
sw.B: Kwa kosa lako mwenyewe utaachilia urithi niliokupa, \q nami nitakufanya uwatumikie adui zako katika nchi usiyoijua; \q kwa maana mmeiwasha hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kama moto utakaowaka milele.
sw.R: Kwa sababu ya mambo uliyoyatenda, utaipoteza nchi niliyokupa uimiliki. \q Nitakufanya uwatumikie adui zako katika nchi ambayo hujawahi kuijua. \q Kwa maana mmewasha moto wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, nao utawaka milele.

vi.L: Chính ngươi sẽ buông mất sản nghiệp mà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho ngươi, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ khiến ngươi phục dịch kẻ thù trong một xứ ngươi không biết; \q vì các ngươi đã nhen lửa trong cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; nó sẽ cháy đến đời đời.
vi.B: Do chính lỗi của ngươi, ngươi sẽ mất sản nghiệp {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho ngươi, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ bắt ngươi phục dịch kẻ thù trong một xứ ngươi không biết; \q vì các ngươi đã làm cho cơn giận {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bừng cháy như ngọn lửa sẽ cháy mãi mãi.
vi.R: Vì những gì ngươi đã làm, ngươi sẽ mất xứ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã ban cho ngươi giữ lấy. \q Ta sẽ bắt ngươi phục dịch kẻ thù trong một xứ ngươi chưa bao giờ biết. \q Vì các ngươi đã nhóm lửa giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và nó sẽ cháy mãi mãi.

ko.L: 너는 스스로 내가 너에게 준 네 유업에서 손을 놓게 될 것이다. \q 내가 네가 알지 못하는 땅에서 너로 네 원수들을 섬기게 하겠다. \q 너희가 내 분노에 불을 붙였으니 그 불이 영원히 탈 것이다.
ko.B: 네가 저지른 일 때문에 너는 내가 너에게 준 유산을 잃을 것이다. \q 내가 네가 알지 못하는 땅에서 너로 원수들을 섬기게 하겠다. \q 너희가 내 분노에 불을 붙였으니 그 불이 영원히 타오를 것이다.
ko.R: 네가 한 일 때문에 너는 내가 너에게 준 땅을 잃을 것이다. \q 내가 네가 전혀 알지 못하는 땅에서 너로 네 원수들을 섬기게 하겠다. \q 너희가 내 분노의 불을 붙였으니 그 불이 영원히 탈 것이다.

pt.L: E tu soltarás, e isso por ti mesmo, a tua herança que eu te dei, \q e te farei servir aos teus inimigos numa terra que não conheces; \q pois vocês acenderam um fogo na {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira; para sempre arderá.
pt.B: Por tua própria culpa, abrirás mão da herança que eu te dei, \q e te farei servir aos teus inimigos numa terra que não conheces; \q pois vocês acenderam a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira como um fogo que vai arder para sempre.
pt.R: Por causa do que fizeste, vais perder a terra que eu te dei para guardar. \q Vou fazer com que sirvas aos teus inimigos numa terra que nunca conheceste. \q Pois vocês acenderam o fogo da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira, e ele vai arder para sempre.

decisions.choice: let go: release your hold on the land, as in the year of release
decisions.reason: The verb means to let something drop or go free. It is the word used for leaving the land unworked in the seventh year (Exodus 23:11) and for releasing debts (Deuteronomy 15:2-3). The people who would not let the land rest will now let go of it altogether, a fitting link to the Sabbath sermon that ends this chapter (verses 19-27; compare Leviticus 26:34-35).

decisions.choice: even by yourself: through your own fault
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "and in you", a short phrase that is hard to explain. It most likely stresses that the loss comes about through the people themselves. Some suggest a small change of letters to read "your hand", "you will let your hand drop from your inheritance".

decisions.choice: your inheritance: the land God gave Israel as its family holding
decisions.reason: The land was Israel's inheritance from God, divided among the tribes and families (Joshua 13-19; Jeremiah 2:7; 12:14-15). To lose it is to lose the gift at the center of the covenant.

decisions.choice: you have kindled a fire in my anger: your sin has set God's anger burning
decisions.reason: God's anger is pictured as a fire that the people themselves have lit. 15:14 has the same picture: "a fire is kindled in my anger".

decisions.choice: Through your own doing / Because of what you have done
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the phrase "even by yourself" first and say plainly what it means (m2).

decisions.choice: "soltarás"
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for letting the land go in the year of release (Deuteronomy 15:2); Literal keeps that sense.

decisions.choice: utaachilia
decisions.reason: "Kuachilia", to release, the word of the year of release (meaning decision m1), so the land is let go as a debt is.

decisions.choice: tu (verses 3-4a); vocês acenderam (4b)
decisions.reason: As in 15:13-14, which these verses repeat (m1 at verse 3), God speaks to the nation as one and then, with a plural verb, to its people: Portuguese keeps "tu" and then "vocês", as it did there.

source.text: כֹּ֣ה׀אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה אָר֤וּר הַגֶּ֨בֶר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִבְטַ֣ח בָּֽאָדָ֔ם וְשָׂ֥ם בָּשָׂ֖ר זְרֹע֑וֹ וּמִן־יְהוָ֖ה יָס֥וּר לִבּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh: cursed [is] the man who trusts in humankind and makes flesh his arm, and from Yahweh turns away his heart.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Cursed [is] {{gender:the person|the man}} who trusts in humankind \q and makes flesh {{gender:their|his}} arm, \q and whose heart turns away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: Cursed is {{gender:the one|the man}} who puts trust in human beings \q and leans on mere flesh for strength, \q whose heart turns away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: Cursed is anyone who trusts in people \q and depends on weak humans for strength, \q anyone whose heart turns away from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: {{gender:Maldita [es] la persona|Maldito [es] el hombre}} que confía en el ser humano \q y hace de la carne su brazo, \q y cuyo corazón se aparta {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: {{gender:Maldita la persona|Maldito el hombre}} que pone su confianza en los seres humanos \q y se apoya en simples mortales para tener fuerza, \q cuyo corazón se aparta {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Maldito todo aquel que confía en la gente \q y depende de seres humanos débiles para tener fuerza, \q todo aquel cuyo corazón se aparta {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Maudit [soit] l’{{gender:être humain|homme}} qui se confie dans l’humain \q et qui fait de la chair son bras, \q et dont le cœur se détourne {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Maudit soit l’{{gender:être humain|homme}} qui met sa confiance dans les humains \q et qui s’appuie sur la chair pour être fort, \q et dont le cœur se détourne {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Maudit soit celui qui met sa confiance dans les gens \q et qui compte sur de faibles humains pour être fort, \q celui dont le cœur se détourne {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Amelaaniwa mtu yule anayemtumainia mwanadamu \q na kuufanya mwili kuwa mkono wake, \q na ambaye moyo wake umegeuka kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Amelaaniwa mtu anayewatumainia wanadamu \q na kuutegemea mwili dhaifu kwa nguvu zake, \q ambaye moyo wake umegeuka kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Amelaaniwa mtu yeyote anayewatumainia watu \q na kuwategemea wanadamu dhaifu ili wampe nguvu, \q mtu yeyote ambaye moyo wake umegeuka kumwacha {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Đáng nguyền rủa thay người tin cậy loài người, \q lấy xác thịt làm cánh tay mình, \q và lòng lìa xa {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Đáng nguyền rủa là người đặt lòng tin cậy nơi loài người \q và nương cậy sức lực của xác thịt, \q là người có lòng lìa xa {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Đáng nguyền rủa là người nào tin cậy con người \q và trông cậy vào sức lực yếu ớt của loài người, \q người có lòng lìa xa {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 사람을 믿고 \q 육체를 자기 팔로 삼으며 \q 그 마음이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 떠난 사람은 저주를 받는다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 사람을 의지하고 \q 연약한 인간의 힘에 기대며 \q 마음이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 떠난 사람은 저주를 받는다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 사람을 믿고 \q 약한 인간의 힘에 기대는 사람은 누구든지 저주를 받는다. \q 마음이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}에게서 떠난 사람은 누구든지 저주를 받는다.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: {{gender:Maldita [é] a pessoa|Maldito [é] o homem}} que confia no ser humano \q e faz da carne o seu braço, \q e cujo coração se afasta {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: {{gender:Maldita é a pessoa|Maldito é o homem}} que põe a sua confiança em seres humanos \q e busca a sua força na simples carne, \q cujo coração se afasta {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} diz: Maldito é todo aquele que confia nas pessoas \q e depende de gente fraca para ter força, \q todo aquele cujo coração se afasta {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.

decisions.choice: cursed ... blessed: the two ways set side by side (verses 5-8)
decisions.reason: Verses 5-8 set two kinds of person against each other, the one who trusts in people and the one who trusts in the LORD, each with a picture from nature. The pattern is that of Psalm 1, where the righteous are like a tree by water and the wicked like chaff, and of the blessing and the curse set before Israel (Deuteronomy 11:26-28; 30:19).

decisions.choice: the person who trusts in humankind: the word for the person is one that stresses human strength, and the one trusted is ordinary humanity
decisions.reason: Two different words are used: the person is a geber, a word that often points to a man in his strength, and the one trusted is 'adam, humankind in general. The saying is about any person who relies on human help, such as alliances with foreign powers (2:36-37), in place of God.

decisions.choice: makes flesh his arm: relies on human power
decisions.reason: The arm stands for strength and power. "Flesh" is human nature in its weakness and frailty, set against God (Isaiah 31:3; 2 Chronicles 32:8).

decisions.choice: the person / the one, with "the man" as the alternative; anyone at Readable
decisions.reason: The saying applies to anyone, man or woman, so it follows the gender setting, as Psalm 1:1-3 does.

decisions.choice: leans on mere flesh for strength / depends on weak humans for strength
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom "makes flesh his arm" (m3).

decisions.choice: "Maldita la persona" / "Maldito el hombre"
decisions.reason: As in the Psalms ("Dichosa la persona" / "Dichoso el hombre"), the gender setting has two Spanish wordings here; Readable says "todo aquel", which covers anyone.

decisions.choice: mtu, wake (no gender span)
decisions.reason: "Mtu" is any person and "wake" is his or her alike, so the English gender spans in verses 5-11 have no Swahili counterpart.

decisions.choice: "l’être humain" (alternative "l’homme") at Literal and Balanced; "celui qui" at Readable; the pronouns after it without a span
decisions.reason: As in the French Psalm 1:1, the noun takes the gender setting and the generic "il", "son" that refer back to it take none.

decisions.choice: "người" with no gender span (verses 5-11)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese "người" is already the person of either sex, and the pronouns that follow ("người ấy", "mình") need no alternative, so the English gender spans of these verses have no Vietnamese counterpart.

decisions.choice: 사람, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean 사람 means any person, man or woman, and Korean needs no pronoun for "he" in verses 5-11, so the English gender spans have nothing to change in Korean.

decisions.choice: {{gender:Maldita é a pessoa|Maldito é o homem}}; "o seu braço", "será", with no span
decisions.reason: The saying is for anyone (r-en-1), so the default is "a pessoa", with "o homem" as the alternative, as Psalm 1:1 has it in Portuguese; the adjective goes inside the span because it agrees with the noun. The English puts "their/his" and "they/he" under the setting too (verses 5-8); Portuguese "o seu" and a verb without a subject are the same for a man or a woman, so those words need no span, as in Psalm 1:2-3.

source.text: וְהָיָה֙ כְּעַרְעָ֣ר בָּֽעֲרָבָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א יִרְאֶ֖ה כִּי־יָב֣וֹא ט֑וֹב וְשָׁכַ֤ן חֲרֵרִים֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר אֶ֥רֶץ מְלֵחָ֖ה וְלֹ֥א תֵשֵֽׁב׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he will be like a juniper in the desert, and not he will see when comes good; and he will dwell [in] parched places in the wilderness, a land of salt and not inhabited.

en.L: And {{gender:they|he}} will be like a juniper in the desert, \q and will not see when good comes; \q {{gender:they|he}} will dwell in parched places in the wilderness, \q a land of salt and not inhabited.
en.B: {{gender:They|He}} will be like a bare shrub in the desert, \q and will not see good when it comes. \q {{gender:They|He}} will live in the scorched places of the wilderness, \q in a salt land where no one lives.
en.R: That person will be like a bush in the desert \q that never sees good things come. \q They will live in the dry, burning wilderness, \q in a salty land where no one can live.

es.L: Será como un enebro en el desierto, \q y no verá cuando venga el bien; \q habitará en sequedales en el desierto, \q tierra salada y deshabitada.
es.B: Será como un arbusto pelado en el desierto, \q y no verá el bien cuando llegue. \q Vivirá en los lugares abrasados del desierto, \q en una tierra salada donde nadie vive.
es.R: Esa persona será como un arbusto en el desierto \q que nunca ve llegar cosas buenas. \q Vivirá en el desierto seco y ardiente, \q en una tierra salada donde nadie puede vivir.

fr.L: Et il sera comme un genévrier dans la steppe, \q et il ne verra pas venir le bonheur ; \q il habitera les lieux brûlés du désert, \q une terre salée et inhabitée.
fr.B: Il sera comme un arbuste dénudé dans la steppe, \q et il ne verra pas le bonheur quand il viendra. \q Il habitera les lieux desséchés du désert, \q une terre salée où personne n’habite.
fr.R: Cette personne sera comme un buisson dans le désert, \q qui ne voit jamais rien de bon arriver. \q Elle vivra dans le désert sec et brûlant, \q dans une terre salée où personne ne peut vivre.

sw.L: Naye atakuwa kama mretemu jangwani, \q wala hataona mema yajapo; \q atakaa mahali palipokauka nyikani, \q nchi ya chumvi isiyokaliwa.
sw.B: Atakuwa kama kichaka kikavu jangwani, \q wala hataona mema yatakapokuja. \q Ataishi mahali palipoungua nyikani, \q katika nchi ya chumvi ambamo hakuna anayeishi.
sw.R: Mtu huyo atakuwa kama kichaka jangwani \q kisichoona kamwe mambo mema yakija. \q Ataishi katika nyika kavu inayounguza, \q katika nchi ya chumvi ambamo hakuna mtu anayeweza kuishi.

vi.L: Người ấy sẽ như cây bách xù trong đồng hoang, \q và sẽ không thấy khi phước lành đến; \q người ấy sẽ ở nơi khô cháy trong hoang mạc, \q một vùng đất mặn không người ở.
vi.B: Người ấy sẽ như bụi cây trụi lá nơi đồng hoang, \q không thấy phước lành khi nó đến. \q Người ấy sẽ sống nơi khô cháy trong hoang mạc, \q trong vùng đất mặn không ai ở.
vi.R: Người ấy sẽ như bụi cây trong sa mạc, \q chẳng bao giờ thấy điều tốt lành đến. \q Người ấy sẽ sống nơi hoang mạc khô cằn nóng bỏng, \q trong vùng đất mặn không ai có thể sống.

ko.L: 그는 사막의 노간주나무 같아서 \q 좋은 것이 와도 보지 못하고, \q 광야의 메마른 곳, \q 사람이 살지 않는 소금 땅에서 살 것이다.
ko.B: 그는 사막의 앙상한 떨기나무 같아서 \q 좋은 일이 와도 보지 못할 것이다. \q 광야의 바싹 마른 곳, \q 아무도 살지 않는 소금 땅에서 살 것이다.
ko.R: 그런 사람은 사막의 덤불과 같아서 \q 좋은 일이 오는 것을 보지 못한다. \q 그는 메마르고 뜨거운 광야에서, \q 아무도 살 수 없는 짠 땅에서 살 것이다.

pt.L: E será como um zimbro na planície deserta, \q e não verá quando vier o bem; \q habitará em lugares ressequidos no deserto, \q terra de sal e não habitada.
pt.B: Será como um arbusto seco no deserto, \q e não verá o bem quando ele vier. \q Viverá nos lugares abrasados do deserto, \q numa terra salgada onde ninguém mora.
pt.R: Essa pessoa vai ser como um arbusto no deserto, \q que nunca vê chegar coisas boas. \q Vai viver no deserto seco e quente, \q numa terra salgada onde ninguém consegue viver.

decisions.choice: a juniper in the desert: a stunted shrub in dry ground
decisions.reason: The word ('ar'ar) names a desert shrub, perhaps a kind of juniper; it sounds like the word for the desert plain ('aravah) beside it. A related word means "destitute" (Psalm 102:18), so the plant is a picture of someone stripped and alone. In 48:6 the same word is used of a shrub in the wilderness.

decisions.choice: will not see when good comes: will not live to enjoy good things, even when they come
decisions.reason: The shrub stays dry even when rain falls elsewhere; so the one who turns from God will miss the good that comes. Verse 8 answers this with the tree that "will not fear when heat comes".

decisions.choice: a land of salt: barren ground where nothing grows
decisions.reason: Salty ground could not be farmed (Deuteronomy 29:22; Judges 9:45; Psalm 107:34). The area around the Dead Sea was the clearest example in Israel.

decisions.choice: they, with "he" as the alternative; That person at Readable
decisions.reason: The verbs refer back to the person of verse 5, who stands for anyone, so they follow the gender setting.

decisions.choice: verbs with no subject pronoun, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish leaves the subject in the verb, so "they" / "he" has no Spanish counterpart here or in verse 8.

pt.R: Bendito é todo aquele que confia {{divine_name:no SENHOR|em Javé}}, \q todo aquele que depende {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.

decisions.choice: blessed: one on whom God's blessing rests
decisions.reason: The word (barukh) is the opposite of "cursed" in verse 5 and speaks of the blessing God gives. Psalm 1:1 uses a different word ('ashrei), "how happy", for the same kind of person.

decisions.choice: trusts ... his trust: the verb and the noun come from the same root
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the root: the one who trusts in the LORD, and the LORD is his trust, the one he relies on. The repetition stresses that his confidence rests on God alone.

decisions.choice: the person / the one, with "the man" as the alternative; anyone at Readable
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

decisions.choice: anayemtumainia ... tumaini lake
decisions.reason: The verb and the noun share one root in Hebrew (meaning decision m2), and Swahili "-tumaini" can do the same.

decisions.choice: Bendito/Bendita (every level)
decisions.reason: The word is barukh, the opposite of "maldito" in verse 5 (m1), so Portuguese says "bendito", the word for one God has blessed; "bem-aventurado" and "feliz" are kept for 'ashrei, Psalm 1:1's word, which the Hebrew does not use here.

source.text: וְהָיָ֞ה כְּעֵ֣ץ׀שָׁת֣וּל עַל־מַ֗יִם וְעַל־יוּבַל֙ יְשַׁלַּ֣ח שָֽׁרָשָׁ֔יו וְלֹ֤א יִרְאֶה֙ כִּֽי־יָבֹ֣א חֹ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה עָלֵ֖הוּ רַֽעֲנָ֑ן וּבִשְׁנַ֤ת בַּצֹּ֨רֶת֙ לֹ֣א יִדְאָ֔ג וְלֹ֥א יָמִ֖ישׁ מֵעֲשׂ֥וֹת פֶּֽרִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he will be like a tree planted by water, and by [a] stream it sends out its roots; and not it will fear when comes heat, and will be its leaves green; and in [a] year of drought not it will be anxious, and not it will cease from producing fruit.

en.L: And {{gender:they|he}} will be like a tree transplanted by water, that sends out its roots by a stream; \q and it will not fear when heat comes, \q and its leaves will be green; \q and in a year of drought it will not be anxious, \q and it will not cease from yielding fruit.
en.B: {{gender:They|He}} will be like a tree set out beside the water, that sends its roots out along a stream. \q It has no fear when the heat comes; \q its leaves stay green. \q In a year of drought it has no worries, \q and it never stops bearing fruit.
en.R: They will be like a tree planted beside the water, with roots that reach out to a stream. \q It is not afraid when the heat comes, \q and its leaves stay green. \q It does not worry when no rain falls for a year, \q and it never stops giving fruit.

es.L: Será como árbol trasplantado junto a las aguas, que extiende sus raíces junto a la corriente; \q y no temerá cuando venga el calor, \q y sus hojas estarán verdes; \q y en año de sequía no se inquietará, \q ni dejará de dar fruto.
es.B: Será como un árbol plantado junto al agua, que extiende sus raíces a lo largo de un arroyo. \q No tiene miedo cuando llega el calor; \q sus hojas siguen verdes. \q En año de sequía no se preocupa, \q y nunca deja de dar fruto.
es.R: Será como un árbol plantado junto al agua, con raíces que llegan hasta un arroyo. \q No tiene miedo cuando llega el calor, \q y sus hojas siguen verdes. \q No se preocupa cuando no llueve en todo un año, \q y nunca deja de dar fruto.

fr.L: Et il sera comme un arbre transplanté près des eaux, qui étend ses racines vers un ruisseau ; \q et il ne craindra pas quand viendra la chaleur, \q et son feuillage sera vert ; \q et dans l’année de sécheresse, il ne s’inquiétera pas, \q et il ne cessera pas de porter du fruit.
fr.B: Il sera comme un arbre mis en terre au bord de l’eau, qui étend ses racines le long d’un ruisseau. \q Il ne craint pas quand vient la chaleur ; \q ses feuilles restent vertes. \q Dans une année de sécheresse, il n’a pas de souci, \q et il ne cesse jamais de porter du fruit.
fr.R: Il ressemble à un arbre planté au bord de l’eau, avec des racines qui vont jusqu’au ruisseau. \q Il n’a pas peur quand vient la chaleur, \q et ses feuilles restent vertes. \q Il ne s’inquiète pas quand il ne pleut pas pendant toute une année, \q et il ne cesse jamais de donner des fruits.

sw.L: Naye atakuwa kama mti uliopandikizwa kando ya maji, unaoeneza mizizi yake kando ya mto; \q wala hautaogopa joto lijapo, \q na majani yake yatakuwa mabichi; \q na katika mwaka wa ukame hautahangaika, \q wala hautaacha kuzaa matunda.
sw.B: Atakuwa kama mti uliopandwa kando ya maji, unaoeneza mizizi yake kandokando ya kijito. \q Hauogopi joto linapokuja; \q majani yake yanabaki mabichi. \q Katika mwaka wa ukame hauna wasiwasi, \q wala hauachi kamwe kuzaa matunda.
sw.R: Atakuwa kama mti uliopandwa kando ya maji, wenye mizizi inayofika hadi kijitoni. \q Hauogopi joto linapokuja, \q na majani yake yanabaki mabichi. \q Hauna wasiwasi mvua isiponyesha kwa mwaka mzima, \q wala hauachi kamwe kuzaa matunda.

vi.L: Người ấy sẽ như cây được trồng bên dòng nước, đâm rễ bên dòng suối; \q nó sẽ không sợ khi nắng nóng đến, \q và lá nó vẫn xanh tươi; \q trong năm hạn hán, nó không lo lắng, \q và không ngừng sinh trái.
vi.B: Người ấy sẽ như cây được trồng bên bờ nước, đâm rễ dọc theo dòng suối. \q Nó chẳng sợ khi nắng nóng đến; \q lá nó vẫn xanh tươi. \q Trong năm hạn hán, nó chẳng lo âu, \q và không bao giờ thôi sinh trái.
vi.R: Người ấy sẽ như cây trồng bên dòng nước, có rễ vươn ra tới dòng suối. \q Nó không sợ khi nắng nóng đến, \q và lá nó vẫn xanh tươi. \q Nó không lo lắng khi cả năm không có mưa, \q và nó không bao giờ ngừng ra trái.

ko.L: 그는 물가에 옮겨 심은 나무 같아서 시냇가로 그 뿌리를 뻗고, \q 더위가 와도 두려워하지 않으며, \q 그 잎이 푸르고, \q 가뭄의 해에도 걱정하지 않으며, \q 열매 맺기를 그치지 않는다.
ko.B: 그는 물가에 심은 나무, 시냇가로 뿌리를 뻗은 나무와 같다. \q 더위가 닥쳐도 두려워하지 않고, \q 잎이 늘 푸르다. \q 가뭄이 든 해에도 걱정하지 않고, \q 열매 맺기를 그치지 않는다.
ko.R: 그런 사람은 물가에 심은 나무와 같다. 그 뿌리는 시냇가로 뻗어 나간다. \q 더위가 와도 두려워하지 않고, \q 잎이 늘 푸르다. \q 한 해 동안 비가 오지 않아도 걱정하지 않고, \q 열매 맺기를 그치지 않는다.

pt.L: Pois será como uma árvore transplantada junto às águas, que estende as suas raízes junto a um ribeiro; \q e não temerá quando vier o calor, \q e as suas folhas estarão verdes; \q e no ano da seca não ficará ansiosa, \q e não deixará de dar fruto.
pt.B: Será como uma árvore posta junto às águas, que estende as suas raízes ao longo de um ribeiro. \q Não tem medo quando chega o calor; \q as suas folhas continuam verdes. \q No ano da seca, não se preocupa, \q e nunca deixa de dar fruto.
pt.R: Essa pessoa vai ser como uma árvore plantada perto da água, com raízes que se estendem até um riacho. \q Ela não tem medo quando chega o calor, \q e as suas folhas continuam verdes. \q Não se preocupa quando passa um ano sem chuva, \q e nunca deixa de dar frutos.

decisions.choice: a tree transplanted by water: the picture of Psalm 1:3
decisions.reason: Psalm 1:3 says the one who delights in the LORD's instruction is "like a tree transplanted by channels of water ... its leaf does not wither". Jeremiah uses the same words for a tree planted by water, and adds the roots reaching to the stream, the heat and the drought.

decisions.choice: it will not fear: the form read aloud (qere)
alternatives: it will not see when heat comes
decisions.reason: The written consonants read "it will not see", the same words used of the desert shrub in verse 6; the scribes marked the reading "it will not fear", which fits the parallel line "it will not be anxious". The meaning hardly changes: the tree is untroubled when the heat comes.

decisions.choice: be anxious: worry, be troubled
decisions.reason: The verb is used of people who worry about what will happen (38:19; 1 Samuel 9:5). The tree is spoken of as if it were a person, untroubled by drought because its roots reach the water.

decisions.choice: transplanted / set out beside / planted beside
decisions.reason: Each level uses the wording of Psalm 1:3 where the Hebrew is the same ("like a tree transplanted" / "set out beside" / "planted beside"). It differs where Jeremiah does: "water" and "a stream" for "channels of water", and leaves that stay green for leaves that do not wither.

decisions.choice: "como árbol plantado junto a"
decisions.reason: The picture of Psalm 1:3; the shared words ("árbol plantado", "su hoja", "da fruto") are kept so the reader can hear the psalm, without copying its sentence.

decisions.choice: uliopandikizwa (Literal); uliopandwa (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The picture of Psalm 1:3 (meaning decision m1); Literal keeps "transplanted", Balanced and Readable say "planted" as the published psalm does.

decisions.choice: "un arbre transplanté" (L); "mis en terre" (B); "planté" (R)
decisions.reason: Each level takes the wording of the French Psalm 1:3 where the Hebrew is the same, so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: "cây được trồng bên dòng nước"
decisions.reason: The picture is that of Psalm 1:3; the same plain words are used so the echo can be heard.

decisions.choice: 물가에 옮겨 심은 나무 (Literal); 물가에 심은 나무 (Balanced)
alternatives: | Psalm 1:3 uses the same picture; Korean keeps the published Psalm's words where the Hebrew is the same, so the link can be seen.

decisions.choice: árvore transplantada junto (L), posta junto (B), plantada perto (R); as suas folhas; dar fruto
decisions.reason: The tree is the one of Psalm 1:3 (m1), and each level keeps the words that verse has in Portuguese: "uma árvore transplantada junto a" (L), "posta junto a" (B), "plantada perto de" (R), "as suas folhas", "dar fruto", and Readable's "Essa pessoa". Where Jeremiah differs, the waters and the stream, the green leaves and the year of drought, Portuguese follows Jeremiah.
